**🚨 issue (security):** Path prefix checks are not portable and can be bypassed on Windows due to hardcoded '/' separators.

These `startsWith(normalizedRoot + '/')` checks rely on POSIX `/`, but `join`/`realpath` return platform-specific paths. On Windows they use `\`, so the prefix check can fail or be bypassed, weakening the traversal protection. Please use `path.resolve` and `path.sep`-aware logic (e.g. `path.relative` or a normalized `root` that ends with `path.sep` and a corresponding `real.startsWith(root)` check). The same adjustment is needed in `validateResolvedPath` and the directory check in `openUploadStream`.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use block IDs, not ETags, in Azure multipart completion**

The multipart completion path currently treats any base64/alphanumeric `etag` as a block ID, but real part ETags commonly also match that pattern. When clients pass back upload ETags (rather than the generated block IDs), `commitBlockList` receives identifiers that were never uploaded by `signMultipartUploadPartUrl`, which causes Azure to reject completion (e.g., invalid block list). This should derive or validate block IDs from `partNumber` instead of trusting generic ETag text.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate upload target path before local write stream creation**

The upload path checks that the parent directory resolves under `rootDir`, but it does not validate the final file path before `createWriteStream`. If a symlink file already exists at that key and points outside the root, Node follows it and writes outside the storage sandbox, bypassing the traversal protection used in the read/delete paths. Add a no-follow file-level check (e.g., lstat/realpath guard) before opening the writer.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stream Azure uploads instead of buffering whole object**

This implementation stores every incoming chunk in memory and concatenates the entire payload on close before uploading. Under large or concurrent uploads, memory usage grows with object size and can trigger process OOMs, which breaks the expected behavior of a `proxyStreamingUpload` adapter. Switching to Azure's streaming upload API (or piping chunks directly) avoids this unbounded buffering.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**`completeMultipartUpload` commits wrong block IDs to Azure** The condition on line 280 is `p.etag.startsWith('block-') || p.etag.match(/^[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+$/)`. The second branch matches virtually every string (hex ETags, base64, alphanumeric), so the `generateBlockId` fallback is unreachable. More critically, the first branch (`p.etag.startsWith('block-')`) passes the *decoded* form (e.g. `'block-000001'`) straight to `commitBlockList`. Azure requires block IDs to be **base64-encoded**. `generateBlockId` correctly returns the base64 form (e.g. `'YmxvY2stMDAwMDAxIwI='`), but the test on line 211 passes `etag: 'block-000001'` (decoded), triggering the first branch and sending a non-base64 string to Azure — causing a `400 InvalidBlockId` error at runtime. The simplest correct fix is to always derive the block ID from the part number, which guarantees the IDs committed here match those embedded in the signed URLs produced by `signMultipartUploadPartUrl`: ```suggestion const sortedParts = input.parts.sort((a, b) => a.partNumber - b.partNumber); const blockList = sortedParts.map(p => generateBlockId(p.partNumber)); await blockBlobClient.commitBlockList(blockList); ```

The second branch matches virtually every string (hex ETags, base64, alphanumeric), so the `generateBlockId` fallback is unreachable. More critically, the first branch (`p.etag.startsWith('block-')`) passes the *decoded* form (e.g. `'block-000001'`) straight to `commitBlockList`. Azure requires block IDs to be **base64-encoded**. `generateBlockId` correctly returns the base64 form (e.g. `'YmxvY2stMDAwMDAxIwI='`), but the test on line 211 passes `etag: 'block-000001'` (decoded), triggering the first branch and sending a non-base64 string to Azure — causing a `400 InvalidBlockId` error at runtime. The simplest correct fix is to always derive the block ID from the part number, which guarantees the IDs committed here match those embedded in the signed URLs produced by `signMultipartUploadPartUrl`: ```suggestion const sortedParts = input.parts.sort((a, b) => a.partNumber - b.partNumber); const blockList = sortedParts.map(p => generateBlockId(p.partNumber)); await blockBlobClient.commitBlockList(blockList); ``` How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. `````

**`openUploadStream` buffers entire file in memory** The `write` sink appends every chunk to an in-memory `Buffer[]` array, and only uploads on `close`. For any file larger than available heap this will either be very slow (GC pressure) or crash the process. Consider uploading through a block-blob append stream or using the SDK's `uploadStream` helper instead: ```typescript import { streamToBuffer } from '@azure/storage-blob'; // or use uploadStream async openUploadStream(input) { const blockBlobClient = containerClient.getBlockBlobClient(input.key); const { writable } = blockBlobClient.uploadStream(/* bufferSize, maxConcurrency, options */); return writable; } ``` Alternatively, `blockBlobClient.uploadStream(readableStream, ...)` accepts a Node.js Readable, which you can bridge from the WritableStream sink without buffering everything.

**`_ctx` parameter is accepted but never read** `runConformanceTests` declares a `_ctx: ConformanceTestContext` parameter (the `_` prefix signals intentional non-use), but the current implementation performs only static structural checks and never exercises actual I/O using the supplied key or test data. If live-I/O conformance tests are planned, the parameter will be needed; if the function will remain static-only, removing the parameter simplifies the API and avoids confusing callers who pass a custom context expecting it to take effect.

1\. Root check uses '/' 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness 
createLocalStorageAdapter mixes platform-dependent normalize()/join() with hard-coded "/" in
root-prefix checks, which can incorrectly reject valid keys on platforms that use "\" separators.
This breaks local storage operations on those platforms by throwing false “path traversal detected”
errors.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description `packages/storage-local/src/adapter.ts` enforces root containment using `startsWith(normalizedRoot + '/')` / `startsWith(root + '/')`, which assumes POSIX separators and is inconsistent with platform-dependent `path.normalize()` output. ## Issue Context This adapter already accounts for `\\..` traversal patterns, indicating it intends to work on Windows as well. ## Fix Focus Areas - Use `path.relative(root, candidate)`-based containment checks (or `candidate.startsWith(root + path.sep)`) consistently in both `resolvePath()` and `validateResolvedPath()`. - Ensure the comparison logic works regardless of path separator. ### Fix Focus Areas (locations) - packages/storage-local/src/adapter.ts[45-77] - packages/storage-local/src/adapter.ts[59-69] ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

2\. Upload symlink gap 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security 
openUploadStream validates only the parent directory realpath and never validates the resolved
file path itself, unlike other methods that call validateResolvedPath(filePath). A file-level
symlink at filePath can bypass the root confinement checks during uploads.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description `openUploadStream()` does not validate the final `filePath` against symlink traversal the way `statObject/deleteObject/openDownloadStream` do, creating an upload-only escape hatch. ## Issue Context Directory-level realpath validation does not guarantee the file path is not a symlink to an external location. ## Fix Focus Areas - Call `validateResolvedPath(filePath)` after `mkdir(dir, { recursive: true })` and before `createWriteStream(filePath)`. - Consider rejecting existing symlink files explicitly (e.g., `lstat` check) before opening the stream. ### Fix Focus Areas (locations) - packages/storage-local/src/adapter.ts[128-141] - packages/storage-local/src/adapter.ts[71-84] ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

3\. Azure multipart commit mismatch 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness 
Azure multipart signing generates a deterministic base64 blockId in the signed URL, but completion
trusts parts[].etag as the committed block id (accepting any base64-ish string), so multipart
completion can commit the wrong identifiers or fail. This can break multipart uploads even when part
signing succeeds.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description Multipart part signing uses `generateBlockId(partNumber)` but completion uses `etag` as the block identifier. This is fragile and can cause incorrect `commitBlockList` calls. ## Issue Context The adapter is stateless; it can deterministically regenerate the exact block IDs from `partNumber` without trusting client input. ## Fix Focus Areas - In `completeMultipartUpload`, build `blockList` from `generateBlockId(partNumber)` for every part (after sorting/validating parts), and do not use `etag` as the block identifier. - If you need to validate, compare provided `etag` to expected blockId and throw on mismatch. ### Fix Focus Areas (locations) - packages/storage-azure/src/adapter.ts[233-256] - packages/storage-azure/src/adapter.ts[259-287] ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
